_what: How the words inside a person's files are read and kept, so search finds what is written inside a PDF, a Word or Excel file, a deck or a text file (src/file-words.mjs). `rows` say which files are read and how, first match wins, matched the way the file viewer matches (parts/ui/show/file-preview/file-viewers.json): a row with `type_prefix` matches a file whose media type starts with it; a row with `extensions` matches a file whose media type names nothing (`unnamed_types`) and whose name ends in one of them. `way` is how its words are read: `as-text` decodes its first `text_bytes` as UTF-8; `converted` hands the file to Workers AI's document conversion (env.AI.toMarkdown), which reads PDF, Office, OpenDocument, Numbers, CSV, HTML and XML into text, for a file of at most `converted_bytes`. A file matching no row is not read. The words are kept as the file's `contents` result ({ text, way, cut }), cut to `kept_characters`, which search indexes and finds (src/search.json lane `contents-words`). New and existing files are read by the store's alarm `per_wake` at a time, `seconds_between_wakes` apart; a file whose reading failed is tried at most `tries` times in all. A new kind of file is a row here, never code. `background_reading` (true by default) is the off switch for the alarm's automatic reading: set false, no new file is read in the background and nothing is sent to the document reader; a person or AI asking for one file's words still gets them.
